newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals slip on yen rebound.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals slip on yen rebound.

text.p: Tokyo precious metal futures settled lower across the board on Wednesday, weighed down by weaker spot prices and the yen's slight rebound against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from nine to 13 yen per gram lower. Most-active benchmark October was down 10 yen at 1,380 yen.
Platinum futures were off early lows as private investors actively hunted bargains later in the day.
Platinum prices ranged from two yen to nine yen per gram lower, with benchmark October finishing two yen down at 1,394 yen.
Bullion was quoted at $380.55/85 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $380.35/85 in New York on Tuesday.
Spot gold drifted within tight ranges during Asian hours, sandwiched by selling by overseas investors and buying by Japanese trade houses in arbitrage trade.

Some traders said spot gold could test a support at $380, led by weak silver prices, but firm physical demand for gold in Asia and technical factors could help gold rebound quickly, even if gold breaks through the support.
In gold futures, price losses were partly offset by bargain-hunting purchases by private investors.
Spot platinum was a tad firmer, quoted at $381.75/382.50 per ounce after opening at $380.25/381.00 in Tokyo.

"Buying by Japanese trade houses absorbed selling interest from overseas. But weak sentiment in spot platinum is intact, partly due to weak global physical demand and abundant supplies," one platinum trader said.
Silver futures ranged from 1.6 yen to 3.4 yen per 10 grams lower. Benchmark October was 2.8 yen lower at 180.7 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from one yen to eight yen per gram weaker. Benchmark October was three yen lower at 424 yen.
